findings.problem: The new validator raises ValueError for any URL that is not http(s), has no hostname, or is a blocked address. It runs on every instance, including disabled ones. startup.py:192 calls ensure_config() before setup_logging(). The ensure_config docstring at triggarr/config.py:345 says pydantic.ValidationError 'continue[s] to propagate uncaught'. So a hand-edited TOML that used to load now aborts with a raw pydantic traceback instead of the friendly loguru error-and-exit path used for TOML decode errors. Examples: a disabled instance with url = "radarr:7878" (urlparse reads 'radarr' as the scheme) or "192.168.1.5:7878" (no scheme). The docstring calls this intended hardening, but there is no friendly exit path for it.

findings.fix_hint: strip a trailing dot and lowercase the hostname before the BLOCKED_HOSTS check; reject all-digit or octal-looking hostnames
findings.problem: validate_arr_url_config checks BLOCKED_HOSTS by exact string. ipaddress.ip_address only parses canonical dotted IPs. So http://169.254.169.254./ and http://metadata.google.internal./ (trailing dot), http://2852039166/ (decimal) and http://0251.0376.0251.0376/ (octal) all fail the ip_address parse. findings.title: Metadata-host blocklist can be bypassed with a trailing dot or a non-dotted IP form

findings.problem: Pydantic ValidationError text includes input_value, here the full URL. At startup this is raised before setup_logging and the redacting sink exist (startup.py:192-198), so it goes to stderr unredacted. In the settings route it is logged via logger.warning('{exc}') at routes.py:600. A URL with userinfo (http://user:pass@host) would expose those credentials. pending: confirm the redacting sink does not scrub URL userinfo and that users put basic-auth credentials in *arr URLs.

agent_notes: The new validator runs unconditionally, including on disabled instances with blank/placeholder/malformed URLs (per the docstring at triggarr/models/config.py:101-103). triggarr/config.py:ensure_config()->load_settings() lets pydantic.ValidationError propagate uncaught (see triggarr/config.py:345,370-373), so any pre-existing config.toml with a disabled instance whose URL now fails this check (non-http scheme, link-local literal, etc.) will crash the whole app at startup rather than just reject that instance. This is an availability/resilience concern, not a classic injection/XSS/auth/secrets vulnerability, and appears to be an intentional, documented design choice ('intended hardening per D-01/D-02') rather than an oversight, so it is noted here rather than filed as a security finding.

The web form submission path (triggarr/web/routes.py:561) already enforces the stricter `validate_arr_url()` (no loopback) before constructing the Pydantic model, so the new relaxed `validate_arr_url_config()` model-level check does not weaken the browser-facing settings flow -- it only adds defense-in-depth for config.toml edited outside the UI, consistent with its stated purpose.

findings.problem: This diff wires the pre-existing `validate_arr_url_config()` helper (triggarr/web/validation.py:111-173, not changed here) into `InstanceConfig.url` as a Pydantic field_validator, so it now runs unconditionally at config-load time. The underlying helper blocks `169.254.169.254` etc. only via exact string match against `BLOCKED_HOSTS` (validation.py:150) and via `ipaddress.ip_address()` parsing of strict dotted-quad/colon-hex literals (validation.py:153-166); anything that doesn't parse as a literal falls through the `except ValueError` branch and is accepted unresolved (validation.py:167-171). A trailing-dot FQDN like `169.254.169.254.` or `metadata.google.internal.`, or a non-dotted-decimal IPv4 representation (e.g. the decimal integer form of 169.254.169.254), fails `ipaddress.ip_address()` and isn't in `BLOCKED_HOSTS`, so it passes validation here even though common resolvers/HTTP stacks normalize it back to the blocked address at connect time.
findings.title: Config-load SSRF validator inherits known hostname-matching bypasses
findings.why_it_matters: If true, a config.toml URL using a trailing-dot or numeric-form metadata address would pass this new startup gate and still reach the cloud metadata endpoint when the *arr HTTP client connects, defeating the hardening this diff is meant to add. This is a pre-existing gap in the untouched helper (config-loading previously had no SSRF check at all, so this diff is still a net tightening on this axis) and is capped accordingly; it is not a defect this diff introduces.

The change adds the first import from the models layer into the web layer: /Users/julianamacbook/triggarr/triggarr/models/config.py:106 does a lazy import of triggarr.web.validation.validate_arr_url_config. The web layer already imports models, for example /Users/julianamacbook/triggarr/triggarr/web/routes.py importing triggarr.models.config, so the models and web packages now each know about the other. The plan explicitly authorizes this. /Users/julianamacbook/triggarr/.planning/phases/71-presentation-rewrite/71-02-PLAN.md:189-190 says: "`from triggarr.web.validation import validate_arr_url_config` (module-level import would risk a circular import; web.validation imports nothing from models)". Line 203 adds: "The new validator uses a local (in-function) `from triggarr.web.validation import validate_arr_url_config`". Under the SAFE rule for deviations the intent doc authorizes, this is not a finding.

No import cycle. /Users/julianamacbook/triggarr/triggarr/web/validation.py imports only ipaddress, re and urllib.parse, and nothing from triggarr. /Users/julianamacbook/triggarr/triggarr/web/__init__.py is empty, so importing triggarr.web.validation does not load triggarr.web.routes or middleware, which do import models. The function-level import is therefore defensive rather than required. A module-level import would also be acyclic today, but the lazy form guards against a future __init__.py re-export creating a cycle. The plan chose this on purpose, so I am not raising it.

Long-term layering suggestion (a note, not a finding): validate_arr_url_config is now a pure, domain-agnostic URL policy used by the config model. Its home in triggarr/web/ is a bit misplaced. Moving it, along with BLOCKED_HOSTS and _BLOCKED_NETWORKS, to a neutral module such as triggarr/url_policy.py would remove the models-to-web edge. It would also let validate_arr_url and validate_arr_url_config share one core with a loopback flag. Today the two are near-duplicates, about 50 lines each, differing only in the loopback check. That is 2 copies, below the rule of three.

Cross-layer lazy imports already exist elsewhere. /Users/julianamacbook/triggarr/triggarr/search/scheduler.py:532 and :538 lazily import from triggarr.web.routes, including the private-named _sync_auth_state. That is a reach-in that predates this diff and is out of scope, so it is not flagged. The new import follows that same lazy style and targets a public function.

Pattern consistency is good. The new validator copies the shape of the existing reject_apikey_in_url field_validator on the same field: @field_validator("url") with @classmethod, raising ValueError so pydantic wraps it as a ValidationError. Pydantic v2 runs same-field validators in definition order, so the apikey check runs first, as the plan requires (71-02-PLAN line 202).

Two validation layers now apply to URLs, and this is consistent. On the settings-save path, /Users/julianamacbook/triggarr/triggarr/web/routes.py:561 runs the strict validate_arr_url, which rejects loopback. At model construction, InstanceConfig runs the relaxed variant. Strict is a subset of relaxed, so a URL accepted by the UI always passes the model. The reverse does not hold: a hand-edited TOML with localhost loads fine, but the UI will reject a re-save of that same URL. That is a product-behavior question, presumably settled by D-01/D-02, and not an architecture finding. The impact and bugs agents may want to confirm it is intended.

agent_notes: Blast radius: InstanceConfig is the per-instance model for every app type (radarr/sonarr/lidarr). The new validator runs wherever Settings/InstanceConfig is built: startup load (startup.py:192 -> config.py:load_settings), the settings POST (routes.py:597 SettingsModel(**new_config)), add-instance (routes.py:790, default url '' which short-circuits to ok), and many test fixtures (tests/conftest.py and others). No public signatures change.

Settings POST path: routes.py:561 already applies the stricter validate_arr_url to every submitted URL, which also blocks loopback. So the model validator never adds a rejection there for submitted URLs. The 'preserve existing instances' branch (routes.py:581-593) round-trips URLs that already passed load-time validation, so there is no new POST-time failure mode.

Asymmetry between the two checks: load accepts loopback (127.0.0.1, ::1, localhost) but the web form rejects it. A user with a hand-edited loopback URL loads fine, but any save from the settings page that resubmits that instance will be refused (303 redirect, warning logged). This behavior predates the diff and comes from routes.py:561, but it is a likely support question.
Validator ordering: reject_apikey_in_url is declared first, so for a URL that fails both checks the apikey error comes first. tests/test_config.py:329-335 covers this ordering.

Accepted-value check: private RFC1918 IPs, Docker service names (radarr), Tailscale 100.x IPv4, https, and subpath/query URLs all still pass. Only non-http(s) schemes, missing hostnames, link-local, unspecified (0.0.0.0, ::), multicast, the 4 BLOCKED_HOSTS, and IPv4-mapped IPv6 versions of those (plus 100.64/10) are rejected, and none of those are documented values.

Performance: negligible. The lazy import inside the validator is a sys.modules lookup after the first call. Validation runs once per instance at load and once per settings POST, with no I/O and no DNS resolution.
No database, schema or migration implications. TOML on-disk format is unchanged.

Verdict: shippable. The one recommended follow-up is impact-1: catch pydantic.ValidationError in ensure_config so a rejected URL produces a friendly, redacted startup error instead of a raw traceback and container restart loop.

findings.fix_hint: In ensure_config, catch pydantic.ValidationError from load_settings and route it to a friendly logger.error + sys.exit(1) that names the offending field path without echoing the input value.
findings.problem: Before this change, a URL in triggarr.toml that was malformed, scheme-less, link-local or pointed at a metadata address still loaded. The failure only showed up per instance at request time, where engine/scheduler catch httpx.HTTPError, and it never showed up for a disabled instance. Now validate_url_ssrf raises inside InstanceConfig construction, during startup.py:192 ensure_config -> config.py load_settings. ensure_config (triggarr/config.py:333-373) only turns TOMLDecodeError/UnicodeDecodeError into the friendly _log_corrupt_config_and_exit path. Its docstring says pydantic.ValidationError 'continue[s] to propagate uncaught' because that case was meant to be a schema bug. __main__.py:44-45 only catches KeyboardInterrupt. So bad user content in the file, such as `url = "localhost:7878"` (urlparse sees scheme 'localhost') or `http://0.0.0.0:7878` on a disabled instance, now ends in an uncaught pydantic traceback and the whole daemon stops, not just that instance. With Docker `restart: unless-stopped` this becomes a crash loop. Rejecting these values matches the stated intent (D-01/D-02) and they were never valid http(s) URLs, so the rejection itself is the control working. The defect is how the failure is surfaced: no friendly loguru error naming the instance and field. Also, setup_logging runs at startup.py:197, after ensure_config, so this traceback is printed before the redacting sink exists. It shows the URL input_value, which may include basic-auth userinfo such as http://user:pass@host. pending: confirm the redacting sink is not installed before ensure_config and that pydantic's error repr includes input_value for this field.
findings.title: A bad URL in a hand-edited config now crashes startup with a raw traceback and can restart-loop the container
findings.why_it_matters: On upgrade, a homelab user whose old config has one bad, possibly disabled, instance URL gets a container that won't start and only a pydantic traceback to explain it. That is a total outage of the daemon, not a degraded instance.

findings.problem: This diff tightens a control: it adds a validator at config load. BLOCKED_HOSTS matching in validate_arr_url_config (triggarr/web/validation.py:150) is an exact string comparison, so a FQDN with a trailing dot ('metadata.google.internal.') or a DNS name that resolves to 169.254.169.254 gets through. Before this diff, nothing at load time blocked those inputs, so these are gaps that already existed and the diff does not introduce them. Plain-IPv4 100.64.0.0/10 is intentionally allowed: _BLOCKED_NETWORKS only applies to IPv4-mapped IPv6, and Tailscale CGNAT addresses keep working. pending: show a trailing-dot or DNS-resolved metadata host reaching an outbound httpx request in a real deployment.
findings.title: New load-time SSRF check, capped note: residual gaps here also existed before this diff
findings.why_it_matters: This is defense in depth only. The validator's docstring already lists DNS rebinding as an accepted residual risk.
